newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi says he will not ask for EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi says he will not ask for EMU delay.

text.p: Italy's Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said he would never ask for a delay in Italy's entry to European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) scheduled to start in 1999.
In a intervew with Rome's La Repubblica newspaper on Saturday Ciampi said, "Postpone entry into Europe. I will never ask for this. This is not much but is definate."

Talk of Italy failing to meet the Maastricht financial criteria in 1997 on which EMU entry is based and also rumours of a plan to delay Italy's entry into EMU have rattled Italian financial markets in recent months.
Ciampi denied that there was a international anti-Italy plan to delay Italy's entry in the EMU.
"Our accounts are true, Brussels knows this," he stressed.
